root_cause: HTTP Response Splitting / CRLF header injection (CWE-113)

v1.ref: git tag v4.3.2 (CVE-2020-5247 fix; YANKED from rubygems, built from tag)

flag.resource: response-header-stream integrity: a split-off header line the app never structurally emitted
flag.placement: per-run token embedded by the PoC into the CRLF payload; materialises in the raw response ONLY when Puma accepts the split-inducing (\r-bearing) header value
flag.detect: flag token substring in the raw HTTP response bytes (server response surface only; request path excluded)

mechanism.summary: Puma writes Rack response header values to the socket. CVE-2020-5247 (v4.3.2) added `headers.reject! { |_k, v| CRLF_REGEX =~ v.to_s }` (CRLF_REGEX=/[\r\n]/) that sanitises ONLY the main response headers. The env['rack.early_hints'] lambda, which emits its own headers, was left unchecked -> CVE-2020-5249 residual. v4.3.3 removed the reject! and applied `possible_header_injection?` (HTTP_INJECTION_REGEX=/[\r\n]/) at all three header-writing sites including the early-hints lambda.
mechanism.original_sink: regular response header (Rack app sets headers['X-Reflected']=input)
mechanism.injected_char: lone CR (\r) — same /[\r\n]/ class both CVEs; the incompleteness is the MISSED SINK (early hints), NOT a missed character
mechanism.guard_line_v2: next if possible_header_injection?(v)  # added inside the early-hints lambda + main loop

evidence.fix_reference: git tag v4.3.2 (CVE-2020-5247 fix; YANKED from rubygems, built from tag); git tag v4.3.3 (CVE-2020-5249 fix)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2020-5249 relates to CVE-2020-5247, which fixed this vulnerability but only for regular responses. If an app allows untrusted input in an early-hints header, an attacker can use a carriage return character to end the header and inject malicious content.

provenance.notes: Built from git tags (puma 4.3.2/3.12.3 yanked from rubygems). Confirmed on real Docker: V0 splits via both sinks; V1 blocks regular-header CRLF (reject!) but early-hints CRLF still splits (residual); V2 blocks both. Same mechanism (CRLF /[\r\n]/), missed sink = early hints.
